title: Paul and Linda McCartney attend Sixties photographic exhibition launch in Bath | 1992
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney attended the launch of Linda’s book Sixties in Bath on 9 October 1992.

The event took place at the Royal Photographic Society, then situated in the Octagon Chapel on Milsom Street in Bath, England. It was open to members of the society, although a large crowd of fans gathered outside the venue.

The book and exhibition, both called Sixties, featured Linda’s works from the 1960s, including shots of stars including The Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, The Doors, Janis Joplin, and many more. The exhibition contained previously unpublished photographs, and focused on primarily on her work prior to her marriage to Paul.

The exhibition and book launch took place on what would have been John Lennon’s 52nd birthday.

I’d like to say thank you all for welcoming us to Bath and thank you all for coming. And rock on Tommy!

It’s like reliving old memories, and distant friends. It’s a very good feeling. I’m very proud of Linda.

There are so many I like. I like the one of me shaking hands with John out of The Beatles. Oh, and I like the one of me naked – but then again, I would do. I like all of them – the kid’s good.

Paul McCartney
Evening Chronicle, 10 October 1992

The Beatles performed at the Pavilion in Bath on 10 June 1963.
